_comment: Accepted cross-platform attribute-effect findings, two kinds. DIVERGENCE ({fixture, platforms}): the control-diff verdict (active = the attribute changed the render, inert = it did not) disagrees across the platforms the attribute is declared for — semantic drift unless a deliberate platform idiom; the reason says which. UNIFORMLY-INERT ({fixture, verdict, declared}): a value the SSoT enumerates changes nothing on ANY platform — either it is the default rendering (say so in the reason) or it is dead/unimplemented everywhere. Unrecorded findings fail `jui conformance gate --cross-effect`; entries the measurement no longer supports are stale and must be pruned (`jui conformance cross-effect --update`). Reason 'unreviewed-initial-measurement' marks the initial-measurement backlog — consume it.

entries.reason: Renderer-environment: the AVD/CI emulator renders Compose blur through software (swiftshader), where the radius delta between the declared value and the default lands under the dhash threshold; web's CSS blur shows it. The android EFFECT is real (effectStyle rows measure active) — only the radius magnitude is sub-threshold in this environment.

Declared default: the fixture writes the platform default, so it renders identically to the attribute-less control BY CONSTRUCTION — the fixture cannot discriminate its own default. (For direction values, the axis gate makes the non-matching axis a default too: rightToLeft on a vertical stack is the natural order.)

MEASURED DIVERGENCE FROM THE DECLARED DEFAULT, narrowed to the ios DYNAMIC half — owner F. Folded 2026-08-07 after B measured the ios codegen face and cleared it. The SSoT declares TabView.showLabels default true, and web is measured obeying it (showLabels__false moves 2968 px against the control while __true moves 0), with android inert as well. B took three emits at the fixture's actual shape (`tabs: [{title}, {title}]`, not `child`) and found sjui codegen already implements the declared default: no attribute emits `Label("One", systemImage: "circle")`, `showLabels: true` emits text that does not differ from it by one byte, and `showLabels: false` emits `Image(systemName:)` with no label. So the codegen face is value-is-default and there is nothing for B to change. Whatever makes the ios TRUE face differ from its control is therefore in the dynamic renderer or in SwiftUI's own TabView chrome — F's half. (B's method note, worth keeping: the first probe used a `child` shape and produced the opposite answer; measuring at the fixture's real shape reversed it. Same class as the codegen-effect --paired trap.) The row drops when an ios TabView without showLabels renders labels. Family: declared-default-divergence.

entries.note: Joined to the alignLeftView row by 51-G: same mechanism, measured — the relative-position spellings are honoured by DynamicConstraintLayoutComponent, and this fixture's parent is a plain View (DynamicContainerComponent), where the spelling is only in the known set. 51-C measured the codegen half independently and agrees: the kjui codegen switches the parent to a ConstraintLayout when a child carries a relative-position spelling (compose_builder.rb#has_relative_positioning_in_children?, modifier_builder.rb:1148), so the family boundary is the same on both android paths. The gap is the whole family of 10 spellings (alignTop/Bottom/Left/RightView + alignTop/Bottom/Left/RightOfView + alignCenterVertical/HorizontalView), not this spelling alone. Owner: G, plan 51 — not expected to close in this train; if it does not, it carries to the next one with the owner named.

adjudicated blur-value-not-derived (ios) + backdrop-collapses-8bit (web/android), joining the already-measured common/effectStyle__prominent row: sjui blur_converter.rb hardcodes `.background(.ultraThinMaterial)` for EVERY value and derives nothing from effectStyle — only Dark/Light/ExtraLight select a `.preferredColorScheme`, and on a host that is already light that selection is itself a no-op, so every spelling in this group photographs the same on ios. Over the fixture's flat backdrop the remaining material scrims quantise into the same 8-bit pixels. Closure: D's high-frequency backdrop fixture makes the values separable, and the spelling canon is open with E (same question as the prominent row). NOTE 2026-08-07: A's in-flight web re-measure already reports these fixtures ACTIVE on web (10000 px against the backdrop control); when that run is committed the recorded platform set changes and the ratchet returns the row for re-adjudication, which is the correct behaviour.
